title: Can missing duplicate runes hide an autokey pattern?
question: Can twenty missed adjacent duplicate runes restore the nonzero difference-diagonal unevenness predicted by one ciphertext-autokey rule?
reader_question: Could missing repeated runes be hiding an autokey pattern in LP2?
summary: For exact adjacent duplicate insertions, all 28 nonzero rune-difference counts are unchanged. Even an artificial 20-count allowance reaches CV 0.066 against the source's 0.40 signal bar.
finding: The pinned transcription yields 9,640 within-word pairs, 60 doublets and nonzero difference CV 0.0608. Physical duplicate restoration leaves that CV invariant for any number of insertions. An exact upper bound allowing 20 freely allocated nonzero-diagonal additions is 0.0656; at 40 it is 0.0717. A separate checker confirms every count and the insertion identity for all 29^3 three-rune contexts.
limitations: This bounds only exact adjacent-duplicate deletion/restoration and the specified ciphertext-autokey difference statistic. The pinned source omits pride.txt, so its English-corpus planted-control numbers and surrogate null are not exactly replayed; a declared synthetic lumpy control passes instead. The source amended its chi-square clause after its first run; the physical invariance does not depend on that clause. Other feedback rules, correlated multi-rune errors and nearly flat plaintext distributions remain outside scope.
next_steps: A proposed alternative must state how it changes nonzero adjacent differences, or specify another feedback equation with a different measurable prediction.

scope.representation: First 55 nonempty '%' segments of the pinned krisyotam_runes.txt, matching source LP2-00–54 labels; within-word adjacent rune indices modulo 29.
scope.procedure: Compute nonzero difference-diagonal counts and CV; insert exact adjacent duplicates algebraically and via exhaustive three-rune contexts. Give an artificial adversary k=0..40 arbitrary additions to the 28 nonzero counts and compute its exact maximal CV. Plant a separate synthetic lumpy ciphertext-autokey versus uniform control.
scope.parameters: 9,640 adjacent pairs, 60 doublets; 28 nonzero diagonals; k=0..40, with the source decision at k=20; CV signal bar 0.40, safe bar 0.30.
scope.exclusions: Source Pride & Prejudice-based control numbers, source surrogate null distribution, plaintext-autokey variants, other feedback equations, off-diagonal transcription errors, and plaintext distributions that are nearly uniform.

review.reviewer: Independent parser, exact allocation bound and exhaustive local insertion check

reproduction.environment: Python 3 standard library; bundled MIT-licensed source files; no network.

visuals.caption: Exact adjacent duplicates cannot change the nonzero difference counts. Even a stronger 20-count allowance stays well below the source's 0.40 signal bar.
